title: "CLI and Metadata Reference"

`src/repo_familiar/cli.py` defines executable command and option behavior. This page is the human-readable command index and the single prose reference for the Bootstrap Metadata schema defined by `src/repo_familiar/metadata.py`.

Run any command with `--help` for its current options:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar <command> --help
```

## Command Index

| Purpose | Commands |
|---|---|
| Discover templates and harnesses | `list-templates`, `list-agent-harnesses` |
| Discover profiles | `list-model-profiles`, `list-tool-profiles`, `list-memory-profiles`, `list-prompt-profiles`, `list-safety-profiles`, `list-privacy-profiles`, `list-repomap-profiles`, `list-sandbox-profiles`, `list-secrets-profiles`, `list-design-profiles`, `list-worktree-profiles`, `list-public-interest-profiles` |
| Discover skills and inspect profiles | `list-skills`, `catalog`, `describe` |
| Generate a repository | `generate` |
| Inspect an existing repository | `advise`, `audit`, `resolve-conflicts` |
| Bootstrap an existing repository | `bootstrap-existing` |
| Add selected assets | `add-skill`, `add-docs`, `add-model`, `add-tool`, `add-memory`, `add-prompts`, `add-safety`, `add-privacy`, `add-repomap`, `add-sandbox`, `add-secrets`, `add-design`, `add-worktree`, `add-public-interest` |
| Check provenance and drift | `check`, `diff-upstream-candidate`, `check-skill-sources` |
| Preview or apply supported refresh | `upgrade` |
| Adopt or promote Managed Surfaces | `attach`, `migrate-template`, `migrate-metadata`, `promote-surface`, `promote-template` |
| Export the Agent Plugins pilot | `export-plugin` |

The [Bootstrap Lifecycle](./bootstrap-lifecycle.qmd) records which commands write, preview, or require a clean worktree. Task guides intentionally show only the commands needed for their outcome.

## Generation Defaults

New `generate` calls default to `python-reproducible`. Select `basic` for the generic scaffold or `static-quarto-application` for the opt-in static Quarto client and FastAPI boundary.

Existing-repository commands use `basic` when the repository has no recorded or explicit template. They do not silently reinterpret an unknown recorded template.

Profiles and skills omitted from the command line can be supplied by concrete template defaults. Use [Profiles and Skills](./profiles-and-skills.qmd) for registry lookup commands.

## Bootstrap Metadata

`.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` is generator-owned metadata, separate from agent runtime files under `.agents/`. Schema v1 records provenance, selected options, and generated assets. Schema v2 adds render context, Managed Surfaces, surface assets, and operation history.

The human-readable schema v2 shape is:

```yaml
schema_version: 2
bootstrap_mode: <new_repository-or-existing_repository>
reference_source:
  type: <git-or-package>
  url: <source-url>
  ref: <tag-or-commit>
generated_at: <iso-8601-timestamp>
generator:
  name: repo-familiar
  version: <version-or-commit>
selected_options:
  template: <template-name>
  agent_harnesses: []
  model_profiles: []
  tool_profiles: []
  memory_profiles: []
  prompt_profiles: []
  safety_profiles: []
  privacy_profiles: []
  repomap_profiles: []
  sandbox_profiles: []
  secrets_profiles: []
  design_profiles: []
  worktree_profiles: []
  public_interest_profiles: []
  sops_age_recipients: []
  skills: []
  docs: quarto
generated_assets:
  - path: <repository-relative-path>
    kind: <asset-kind>
    source: <canonical-source>
    content_sha256: <sha256>
render_context:
  project_name: <project-name>
  project_description: <project-description>
  template: <template-name>
  docs: quarto
  selected_options_sha256: <sha256>
  source: generation_inputs
managed_surfaces: []
managed_surface_assets: []
history: []
```

The metadata file is not self-hashed. `content_sha256` is optional when an asset has no checksum baseline and is omitted for the metadata file itself. Existing-repository metadata records only assets written or explicitly adopted by that operation; skipped conflicts remain user-owned.

Valid v1 files stop after `generated_assets` and remain readable. `migrate-metadata` creates v2 render and surface records only from ownership already represented by v1; it does not infer ownership of other repository files.

## Managed Surfaces

Metadata v2 uses explicit Managed Surfaces for adoption and promotion:

- `migrate-metadata` previews or applies a lossless v1-to-v2 migration; unrecorded files remain user-owned.
- `attach` records a metadata-only surface attachment and does not rewrite surface files.
- `migrate-template` previews target surfaces and file states without applying them.
- `promote-surface` applies one checksum-safe, atomic surface promotion without changing the selected template.
- `promote-template` applies all conformable target surfaces as one dependency-ordered transaction and changes the selected template only in the final committed metadata.

Edits, conflicts, extra managed assets, and manual-review strategies can block promotion. Missing target files are eligible for creation; broad promotion never deletes an omitted current surface. See [ADR 0010](../project-record/adr/0010-metadata-v2-preview-first-refresh.md) and [ADR 0012](../project-record/adr/0012-python-first-greenfield-existing-repository-boundary.md) for rationale.

Managed Surface records contain an `id`, version, template, state, comparison basis, strategy, render-context checksum, and the render inputs needed for comparison. Surface-asset records contain a surface ID, path, state, comparison basis, strategy, and optional content checksum.

| Field vocabulary | Values |
|---|---|
| Surface or asset state | `written`, `adopted`, `edited`, `skipped`, `conflict` |
| Strategy | `replace_if_unchanged`, `line_union`, `merge_preview_only`, `manual_review`, `unavailable` |
| History record | `id`, `at`, `command`, `mode`, and optional `surface_id` |

## Generated Asset Authority

Canonical templates plus `src/repo_familiar/asset_plan.py` define generated asset composition. Generator plan output exposes the exact inventory for one selection, and tests verify it. Documentation describes categories and inspection methods rather than copying a full file list that can drift.
